topic: database cardinality estimation; conjunctive query evaluation; degree constraints; information-theoretic bounds
status: bounded theory-to-systems evaluation lead based on one sampled PODS 2025 paper and targeted 2026 primary follow-up checks; novelty not established
claim: For simple degree constraints (|X|≤1), the sampled paper computes the polymatroid cardinality bound in polynomial time and constructs a polynomial-length proof sequence for PANDA. Yet several nearby mixed constraint classes are as hard as general inputs. The tractability boundary should not be generalized to arbitrary statistics. Later systems provide distinct comparison points: PANDAExpress targets downstream evaluation runtime, while CorrBound incorporates richer inter-/intra-relation correlations. A useful next test is a common-workload comparison of bound tightness, plan quality, and compute cost across these axes.
positive_evidence: Theorem 1.1 gives a polynomial-size LP for the polymatroid bound on simple degree constraints; Theorem 1.2 gives proof-sequence length O(k²n²+kn³).
Theorem 1.5 introduces a polynomial-time flow-bound relaxation for arbitrary degree constraints and proves it is at least as tight as the chain bound under a given variable order.
Theorem 1.3 proves hardness persists for unions of simple and acyclic/FD constraints and for constraints with |X|≤2, |Y|≤3; the general complexity remains open.

Primary 2026 records describe PANDAExpress as a downstream query-evaluation algorithm and CorrBound as an estimator using richer correlation statistics, so they motivate a comparative experiment rather than invalidate the sampled theorem.
counterevidence: The paper itself states the general polymatroid-bound complexity remains unresolved and provides tractable relaxations; no claim that practical cardinality estimation is generally intractable follows.
CorrBound and PANDAExpress solve related but non-identical problems and do not constitute direct head-to-head evidence against the sampled simple-degree algorithm.
No optimizer integration, real workload, or runtime experiment was reproduced in this audit.

sources.title: CorrBound: Cardinality Estimation Accounting for Inter- and Intra-relation Correlations
sources.sections: Primary publication abstract; correlation features and benchmark evaluation

falsifiable_test: On identical query/data snapshots, compute simple-degree polymatroid bounds, the flow bound, and a correlation-aware estimator where its required statistics are available; then feed each estimate into the same optimizer. Measure upper-bound tightness, q-error where applicable, plan regret, join runtime, estimator runtime, memory, and statistics collection overhead. The lead weakens if richer statistics add cost without improving plans, or if simple bounds already yield equivalent plans; strengthens if added correlations consistently reduce plan regret at manageable overhead. No implementation or experiment was run.
limitations: The sampled source is theoretical and follow-up checks used primary records/abstracts rather than a full survey of each 2026 algorithm. This is not a novelty claim; estimator values and optimizer outcomes were not reproduced.

topic: database index tuning; LLMs; SQL Server; query performance regression; validation cost
status: bounded systems lead from one sampled PVLDB 2026 full text; novelty not established
claim: On SQL Server 2022 with TPC-H SF10 and four enterprise workloads, GPT-5's best recommendation among five independent calls can substantially beat DTA for a meaningful subset of single-query cases, particularly where optimizer-cost errors mislead DTA. But the model's per-call quality varies substantially; DTA is more stable on the study's constructed multi-query workloads, directly injecting LLM candidates into DTA often degrades results, and physical validation/index creation can cost more than tuning. The evidence supports a candidate-generation-plus-budgeted-validation hypothesis, not stable LLM replacement of a commercial advisor.
positive_evidence: The study uses four anonymized real-world customer workloads with views/CTEs and manually created indexes, plus TPC-H SF10, and measures actual SQL Server 2022 query execution time.

Each prompt receives five independent GPT-5 calls; the paper shows best-of-five recommendations can outperform DTA substantially for some single-query cases and gives examples tied to optimizer cost misestimation.

The paper documents large call-to-call variability, DTA's more reliable performance on its constructed multi-query cases, negative outcomes when enlarging DTA's candidate pool with LLM indexes, and the high cost of physical validation.
counterevidence: The best-of-five comparison selects using measured outcomes and is not the same as a single-call deployable policy; paying for generation and validation changes the end-to-end objective.
Only one commercial DBMS, one chosen LLM (GPT-5 in reported results), four enterprise workloads, and one public benchmark are evaluated; results may not transfer to other systems/workloads/models.
The paper's real workloads are anonymized and the full industrial data may not be independently reproducible; actual execution runs are capped at five minutes, so timeouts are censored observations.

sources.sections: Methods, Findings 1–11, multi-query case studies, validation-cost analysis, conclusion

falsifiable_test: On frozen, non-public-to-the-model workloads across multiple DBMSs, compare DTA alone, one-call LLM, median-of-k, best-of-k, and a cost-aware sequential selection policy. Charge model calls, index creation, query execution, and rollback; stratify by query count/skew and DTA-versus-LLM cost-estimation disagreement. Report speedup, regression tail-risk, storage, tuning latency, and validation budget. The lead weakens if any value of k is dominated once total cost is charged; strengthens if a stopping policy captures most best-of-k gains with lower validation cost and controlled regression risk. Not run.
limitations: One PVLDB study; not independently rerun, no customer data released in this audit, and conclusions are model/version/DBMS/workload-specific. No novelty claim.

topic: multimodal databases; explicit world models; LLM counterfactual reasoning; reproducibility
status: bounded replication-design lead from one sampled arXiv preprint; empirical result explicitly preliminary; novelty not established
claim: DaoQL's theorem establishes a sufficient structural condition for composable counterfactual evaluation under independent rules, deterministic evaluation, and fixed conflict resolution. Its reported empirical gap (94% vs 45%) compares DaoQL+GPT-4o with GPT-4o alone across 1,250 prompts generated from only 250 base scenarios (five paraphrases each). The result is preliminary because prompts, temperature, full scoring rules, and per-case logs are missing. A replication must cluster inference at the scenario level and isolate structured state semantics from retrieval, prompt, and system changes before interpreting the score as a general counterfactual-reasoning gain.
positive_evidence: The paper states a formal sufficient-condition theorem for composable counterfactual decomposability with explicit assumptions, separating theoretical claim from empirical claim.
The experiment covers five domains and reports 94% vs 45% on composable decomposability; other listed metrics include update correctness and traceability.

The paper explicitly labels the empirical validation preliminary and discloses missing full prompts, temperature, scoring protocol, and per-case error logs; it also identifies scale, concurrency, nonofficial LDBC, and single synthetic ANN dataset limitations.
counterevidence: The system is implemented and the paper reports real database/benchmark measurements; limited documentation does not erase the observed results.

Five paraphrases per base case may be useful for testing linguistic robustness, so clustering does not imply discarding the paraphrase-level analysis; it changes uncertainty estimates and generalization claims.
The formal theorem can support a precise architectural property even if the empirical comparison is under-specified.

sources.sections: Theorem 1, counterfactual experiment design/results, scope table, limitations

falsifiable_test: Re-run with preregistered prompts and deterministic rule/state specifications, at least two matched baselines (GPT-4o alone and retrieval/RAG with the same source facts), blinded scoring, released per-scenario logs, and multiple independent base cases per domain. Report both paraphrase robustness and scenario-clustered confidence intervals; ablate explicit state, deterministic Eval, and conflict resolution separately. The lead weakens if the gap vanishes under matched information and scenario-level inference; strengthens if it persists across held-out scenarios and evaluators. Not run.
limitations: One arXiv preprint and no source-code or raw-data audit. The observed 94/45 values are reported, not independently reproduced; five paraphrases from one case are correlated and are not counted here as five new independent scenarios.
